diagnoses: Strict NIO baseline and repeated transport closure terminate with the existing scheduling-after-shutdown fatal error.
Cancellation plus channel close must be followed by joining executeThenClose owners, with one shared shutdown task for repeated/concurrent callers.

A regression caught unbounded server closure with a cancellation-ignoring router call. A cancellation-aware reply box now separates that work from the NIO scope; late replies retain no channel or writer.

Both fake B4 entry points use HTTPServer.server_bind, whose unused getfqdn call matches GitHub's independently reproduced macOS26 loopback resolver stall. Negative tests catch that call; a controlled35-second injection reproduces its cost.
